main_body: Two-storey timber-frame house: a hipped red tile roof over a half-timbered plaster upper storey and a cobblestone ground floor with a wooden door, windows and a hanging sign
top_band: Terracotta tile roof slope, rows 1-43, orange highlight tiles at the top (rows 2-5) shading to dark red-brown at the eave; the hip side slopes are also visible
evidence: In a centre column the roof slope is a large tiled surface (rows 1-43), ending in a dark eave line at rows 43-45. Below it come the plaster and timber upper wall (rows 45-75), a grey ledge and beam at rows 74-77, and the cobble wall (rows 78-106). The roof clearly reads as a top surface, as in the reference houses, and the eave casts a dark shadow on the wall. Windows have frames, sills and flower boxes, and the door has a dark frame. The hip side slopes confirm the roof surfaces. The wall is a south face, not an isometric side face.

style.evidence: The roof has per-tile highlights across about 5-6 steps. The cobblestones are shaded one by one in cream, mauve and dark purple. The plaster carries speckle dots, and the timber has dark brown tinted grain. Outlines are dark brown or red-brown beside the materials, not black. The window and door details and the sign add information. The piece matches the references in richness and has no large flat fills.
